expectations.evidence: `ls` on outputs/ confirms all six directories exist: wiki/ (with index.md, summaries.md, overview.md, auth/, claims/, synthesis/, templates/), raw/auth/, graph/edges.jsonl, audit/{open,resolved}/, log/{events.jsonl, daily/}, outputs/{queries/, reports/}.

expectations.text: Source file is copied to raw/ directory
expectations.evidence: outputs/raw/auth/architecture.md exists (3513 bytes) and contains the full original architecture doc (headings: JWT Access Tokens, Server-Side Sessions, Refresh Flow) matching the fixture described in report.md Phase 0. events.jsonl records bytes_in=3513 matching the file size.

expectations.text: A wiki page is created with proper frontmatter (title, type, tags, sources, created, updated, summary)
expectations.evidence: outputs/wiki/auth/authentication.md frontmatter (lines 1-14) has all seven required fields: title='Authentication and Session Management', type='concept', tags (6 items), sources=[raw/auth/architecture.md], created=2026-04-14, updated=2026-04-14, summary (multi-line block). Also carries a quality:0.0 field.

authentication.md line 4: `tags: [authentication, jwt, session-management, refresh-token, rs256, postgresql]`. All six are content concepts — no structural (e.g., 'concept', 'index'), temporal (e.g., '2026'), or metadata tags. Explicitly contains the three examples named in the assertion.

expectations.text: summaries.md is updated with the new page's summary
expectations.evidence: Both outputs/summaries.md and outputs/wiki/summaries.md contain an '## Authentication' section linking to `auth/authentication.md` with a paragraph summarizing the hybrid RS256 JWT + PostgreSQL session design and per-page tag list. Not a scaffold stub.

expectations.text: Query answer includes inline citations to wiki pages
expectations.evidence: outputs/outputs/queries/2026-04-14-how-does-authentication-work.md contains 9 inline citations linking back to wiki pages, including section-anchor cites like `[auth/authentication.md § JWT Access Tokens](../../wiki/auth/authentication.md#access-tokens-jwt--rs256)`, `[auth/authentication.md § Server-Side Sessions]`, `[auth/authentication.md § Refresh Flow]`, and `[overview.md](../../wiki/overview.md)`. Plus a Citations section at the bottom.

outputs/outputs/queries/2026-04-14-how-does-authentication-work.md (5255 bytes) archived with YAML header recording the query, asked_at, pages_considered, pages_loaded, and relevance_scores. events.jsonl query event's answer_path field points to this same file.

expectations.text: events.jsonl records init, ingest, and query operations
expectations.evidence: outputs/events.jsonl (and log/events.jsonl) only contain two events: `op: ingest` and `op: query`. No `op: init` entry is present. Grep for `init` in both copies returns no matches. The init_wiki.ts script does not emit an init event by design — the scaffold was created but the operation was not logged.

claims.claim: Ingest created wiki page at wiki/auth/authentication.md with quality 0.90 after Mermaid + frontmatter + tags
claims.evidence: authentication.md contains 6-tag frontmatter, two Mermaid blocks (sequenceDiagram for refresh flow, erDiagram for users/sessions/refresh_tokens), 'How to Go Deeper' section, and Related Pages cross-links — consistent with the 0.9 score reported in report.md Phase 3.
events.jsonl query event fields: tokens_in=2088, tokens_out=1313, reduction_ratio=0.918 match report.md Phase 4 verbatim.

claims.claim: EXTRACTED-provenance edge written for wiki->raw source
claims.evidence: graph/edges.jsonl: `{"from":"wiki/auth/authentication.md","to":"raw/auth/architecture.md","type":"supports","provenance":"EXTRACTED","detail":"Wiki page compiled from this source doc."}` — single edge matching the security/provenance contract.

claims.claim: Cache hit was false on first ingest with sha256 8b46715a... matching raw file
claims.evidence: ingest event records cache_hit=false and sha256=8b46715a749941aea3fb046a220a351c03f0f8b101e2a1809b0217ddca33e60e; first ingest of a new file should always miss.

claims.claim: Lint pass cleared 3 auto-fixable errors (missing frontmatter on scaffold stubs)
claims.evidence: index.md, summaries.md, overview.md all now carry full YAML frontmatter (title, type, tags, sources, created, updated, quality, summary) — consistent with the auto-fix pass described in report.md Phase 3. No verification via raw lint output (not in outputs), but the post-state is correct.

suggestions.assertion: events.jsonl records init, ingest, and query operations
suggestions.reason: The skill's init_wiki.ts script does not emit an init event — only ingest and query are logged. Either update the skill so init logs an op (matching this assertion) or relax the assertion to only require ingest+query. As written, this assertion fails even on a correct execution.

suggestions.assertion: A wiki page is created with proper frontmatter (title, type, tags, sources, created, updated, summary)
suggestions.reason: Assertion checks presence of fields but not that values are well-formed. A page with `title: ''`, `type: foo`, `tags: []`, `sources: []` would pass. Consider asserting tag count is within 4-8, type is one of the allowed values (concept/index/synthesis/claim/template), and sources is non-empty for concept pages.

suggestions.assertion: Query answer includes inline citations to wiki pages
suggestions.reason: No assertion checks that the answer is actually grounded in the ingested source — a hallucinated page of plausible JWT copy with fake links to nonexistent pages would still pass. Consider asserting citations resolve to actual files that exist in wiki/ AND that key facts in the answer (RS256, 15-minute expiry, `sessions` table, /auth/refresh) appear in the source.

No assertion checks that the graph/edges.jsonl edge was written with required provenance (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS) — this is a core security/provenance guarantee of the wiki contract but is uncovered.

eval_feedback.overall: 9/10 pass. The one failure is on the 'events.jsonl records init' assertion, which appears to be a mismatch between eval and skill design rather than a real execution defect. Evals would benefit from stricter content-correctness checks on frontmatter values, citation resolution, and provenance-tagged edges.
